item.title: China hands over remains of U.S. airmen found along WWII Hump Route
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
A transfer ceremony of the U.S. service members' remains along the Hump Route is held in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, Nov. 10, 2026. The Chinese and U.S. militaries on Tuesday held a ceremony in Chengdu where China handed over the remains of U.S. airmen who aided China's resistance against Japanese aggression during World War II (WWII), according to China's Ministry of National Defense. The remains were recovered in areas along the Hump Route, a vital air corridor over the Himalayas that became a wartime lifeline for China. From 1942 to 1945, the route served as a key channel for Allied supplies to support China's resistance against Japanese aggression. (Xinhua/Xu Bingjie) CHENGDU, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese and U.S. militaries on Tuesday held a ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, where China handed over the remains of U.S. airmen who aided China's resistance against Japanese aggression during World War II (WWII), according to China's Ministry of National Defense. The remains were recovered in areas along the Hump Route, a vital air corridor over the Himalayas that became a wartime lifeline for China. From 1942 to 1945, the route served as a key channel for Allied supplies to support China's resistance against Japanese aggression. ■

item.title: China welcomes U.S. debut of new giant panda pair
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday he was delighted that a new pair of Chinese giant pandas have recently made their debut before the American public, bringing more joy to the American people. Guo made the comments at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on the public debut of a pair of Chinese giant pandas sent to the United States after Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to the country in September. On Sept. 24, Xi announced during his visit that a pair of pandas would be sent to Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people. The pair, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, arrived on Sept. 27. Before meeting the public last week, they spent more than a month in quarantine, adjusting to the new bamboo, new caretakers and new environment. To ensure the giant pandas' health and safety, a smooth departure from China and their adaptation to the new environment, China and the United States have made full preparations in strict compliance with the requirements and technical standards for international giant panda conservation cooperation, according to Guo. "We believe the new round of cooperation will further contribute to enhancing the conservation capacity for giant pandas and other endangered species, advancing global biodiversity conservation, and deepening the friendship between the Chinese and American people," he said. ■

item.title: China's foreign trade growth picks up pace on stellar imports, booming AI demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign trade in goods maintained strong growth momentum in the first 10 months of 2026, with imports posting especially robust gains and booming artificial intelligence (AI) demand lifting exports of electronic components, official data showed Tuesday. Total imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year to 44.81 trillion yuan (about 6.67 trillion U.S. dollars) over the period, accelerating from 18.8 percent in the first nine months, according to the General Administration of Customs (GAC). Imports surged 23.6 percent, while exports rose 17.6 percent during the January-October period. China's foreign trade has kept up its momentum this year, showing greater resilience and vitality, said Lyu Daliang, director of the GAC's Department of Statistics and Analysis. Both imports and exports have now posted double-digit growth for six consecutive months through October, the customs data showed. In October alone, goods trade expanded 31.2 percent. Notably, imports have been a standout feature this year. "In the first 10 months, China's imports from more than 150 countries and regions recorded growth. Imports from ASEAN, Latin America and Africa all reached record highs for the same period," Lyu said. "China's vast market continued to offer 'China opportunities' to the world." On the export side, mechanical and electrical products played a prominent role with a 25.2 percent increase over the period, accounting for 64.7 percent of total exports, up 3.9 percentage points from a year earlier. Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Golden Credit Rating, said multiple factors kept export growth elevated in October, noting that the global AI investment boom continued to push up prices of chips and other electronic components and computer parts, driving strong growth in export value. Moreover, domestic manufacturing upgrades in recent years have also enhanced the competitiveness of new energy vehicles and high-tech products, Wang said. Smart and green products were among the fastest-growing categories. Exports of integrated circuits and memory components surged 101.9 percent and 132.5 percent, respectively, while 3D printers, digital cameras and industrial robots rose 104.8 percent, 41.4 percent and 17.8 percent. Exports of China's "new three" -- electric vehicles, photovoltaic products and lithium batteries -- grew 46.5 percent, electric motorcycles and bicycles rose 33.3 percent, and wind turbines and their components gained 19.7 percent. By trading partner, China's trade with ASEAN grew 24.2 percent in the first 10 months, while trade with the European Union rose 8.5 percent and trade with the United States expanded 6.3 percent. Trade with Belt and Road participating countries grew 18.5 percent over the same period. Looking ahead, experts believe the strong exports will extend through to the end of the year. As the AI cycle remains in an upswing, China will continue to benefit as a global hub of electronics supply chains, Zhang Di, a macro analyst at China Galaxy Securities, said. The ongoing global green and low-carbon transition, combined with China's rising competitiveness in mechanical equipment, will sustain strong growth in new energy vehicles, ships and other transport machinery, Zhang added. ■

item.title: China issues revised regulations on management of foundations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating revised regulations on the management of foundations. The revised regulations, which consist of 79 articles in eight chapters, will take effect on Jan. 1, 2027. The regulations aim to strengthen the credibility of foundations and promote their sound and orderly development. They stipulate that foundations engaged in public welfare activities must follow the principles of legality, voluntariness, good faith, openness, transparency and non-profit operation. To improve the registration management system, the regulations clarify the registration authority level and registered capital, steadily advance direct registration, specify procedural requirements for registration changes, and refine liquidation procedures prior to deregistration. Highlighting the need to regulate the activities of foundations, these regulations improve requirements for fundraising, donation and grant-making activities, and regulate internet public fundraising and cooperative public fundraising, among others. The regulations also stress the need to improve internal governance, strengthen information disclosure and industry self-regulation, and enhance supervision. ■

item.title: Book of Xi's discourses on poverty reduction, alleviation published
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- A compilation of discourses by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on poverty reduction and alleviation has been published by the Central Party Literature Press and released nationwide. Compiled by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, the book brings together 55 important articles by Xi on poverty reduction and alleviation. Some of these works are made public for the first time. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core has placed poverty alleviation high on its governance agenda and regarded it as the bottom line task in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects. China has won a complete victory in the fight against poverty and accomplished the arduous task of eliminating absolute poverty, creating a miracle in the human history of poverty reduction. In the process, the country has blazed a poverty reduction path and formed an anti-poverty theory with Chinese characteristics. Xi's discourses on poverty reduction and alleviation represent an important theoretical achievement in China's poverty alleviation efforts and the latest achievement in adapting Marxist anti-poverty theory to the Chinese context. These discourses provide important guidance for consolidating and expanding the achievements in poverty alleviation and advancing rural revitalization across the board, promoting modernization that delivers common prosperity for all, and building a better world free from poverty and featuring shared prosperity. ■

item.title: Xi's reply inspires Australian students to carry forward friendship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
As spring unfolds in the Southern Hemisphere, a message of friendship has crossed the ocean. Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to 110 young Australian students who had written to him, encouraging them to remain committed to promoting the China-Australia friendship.
